elements.quote: Through an integrative review, we aimed to identify approaches to evaluate the sustainability of evidence-based interventions (EBIs) and sustainability outcomes.
elements.reason: The abstract identifies the review type as an “integrative review,” but it does not explicitly identify the report as a “systematic review.”

elements.quote: Through an integrative review, we aimed to identify approaches to evaluate the sustainability of evidence-based interventions (EBIs) and sustainability outcomes.

elements.quote: Included studies were not restricted by research design; and had to evaluate the sustainability of an EBI in a healthcare context.
elements.reason: The abstract provides limited inclusion criteria (no restriction by design; must evaluate sustainability in a healthcare context) but does not provide explicit main inclusion and exclusion criteria.
The abstract does not identify information sources with the search dates (e.g., which databases and when each was last searched).

elements.quote: We assessed the methodological quality of studies using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the tool used to assess methodological quality (risk of bias-related assessment).

elements.quote: Methods: Following Whittemore and Knafl's methodological process: (1) problem identification; (2) literature search; (3) data evaluation; (4) data analysis; and (5) presentation, a comprehensive search strategy was applied across five databases.
elements.reason: The abstract describes the review process and analysis approach (data evaluation/analysis/presentation) and indicates the search strategy.

elements.quote: Results: Of 18,783 articles retrieved, 64 fit the inclusion criteria.
elements.reason: The abstract provides the total number of included studies (64) and some characteristics (e.g., qualitative designs, timing frequency), but does not report total number of participants.

elements.quote: Of the 64 studies, 44% used a framework, 26% used a model, 11% used a tool, 5% used an instrument, and 14% used theory as their primary approach to evaluate sustainability. Most studies (77%) did not measure sustainability outcomes, rather these studies focused on sustainability determinants.
elements.reason: The abstract reports quantitative results related to sustainability evaluation approaches and whether outcomes were measured, but it does not clearly present results for each main outcome with the number of studies/participants per outcome.
The provided abstract evidence does not indicate that a meta-analysis was conducted.
The provided abstract evidence does not indicate that groups were compared (no effect direction or favored group reported).

elements.quote: Discussion: It is unclear which approach/approaches are most effective for evaluating sustainability and what measures and outcomes are most commonly used. There is a disconnect between evaluating the factors that may shape sustainability and the outcomes approaches employed to measure sustainability.
elements.reason: The abstract discusses limitations/uncertainty in the included evidence (unclear effectiveness and mismatch between determinants and outcomes).

elements.quote: Our review offers methodological recommendations for sustainability evaluation research and highlights the importance in understanding mechanisms of sustainability to advance the field.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation and discusses implications for future research.
No primary source of funding is reported in the provided abstract evidence.
No registry name and registration number are reported in the provided abstract evidence.

elements.quote: Discussion: It is unclear which approach/approaches are most effective for evaluating sustainability and what measures and outcomes are most commonly used.
